static_traits.name: He Nan
static_traits.family_status: Lives alone, with no immediate family nearby
static_traits.social_status: Having a few friends to talk to, but not fully sharing negative thoughts with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received before
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, strong logic, high cooperativeness, positive attitude; speaking speed not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I often have catastrophic thinking, for example believing that if it does not snow, my whole weekend will be ruined.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent negative and catastrophizing thinking has begun to affect my mood, sleep, and overall enjoyment of life, so I seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Catastrophizing thinking began to appear in adolescence; in recent months it has been more frequent during work scheduling (consecutive night shifts) and plan changes; whenever routines or plans change (such as weather not matching expectations), anxiety and frustration are triggered; the client has not received psychological counseling before and has no major physical illness.

core_beliefs: Things must go according to plan, or the outcome will be terrible
I find change and uncertainty hard to bear

special_situations.event: Weekend weather did not snow, causing the planned outdoor plan and expectations to be affected
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the weather does not match my expectations, I cannot enjoy the weekend
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to push away or deny negative thoughts, and rigidly binds weekend activities to 'snowy outdoor activities'

special_situations.event: Being assigned consecutive night shifts or having the schedule temporarily changed, disrupting daily routine and plans
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as plans change, I will lose control and be unable to cope
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Maintaining a strict and rigid personal plan, trying to avoid flexible adjustments
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The plan has changed, I will definitely have a breakdown in condition, this whole week is ruined.

special_situations.event: Due to working through the night, lacks time for hobbies and leisure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If unable to engage in the preferred hobby, cannot relax and the weekend has no enjoyment
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring other optional activities and possible positive aspects, clinging to a single preference
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be trapped at home, the whole weekend will be boring and frustrating.

core_conflict.wish: Longs for control and stability, to enjoy life and rest according to plan
core_conflict.fear: Fearing change and uncertainty will bring loss of control and a 'completely terrible' outcome
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control and safety by adhering to a strict plan and denying negative thoughts

object_relations.self_representation: Needing predictability, an individual who easily feels helpless when plans are disrupted
object_relations.object_representation: Others who do not understand one's own emotions and state (friends/others)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When negative thoughts are brought up or real-life plans/routines are disrupted
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands change as an uncontrollable threat, believing thoughts must be eliminated quickly to avoid collapse
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Verbally emphasizes 'this is not real / it is nothing', quickly shifts the topic to concrete plans or weather details, with a rather hurried tone to avoid emotional-level discussion.

manifestations: Night-shift work limits personal time and room for choice
Once a plan changes, feels a loss of control, with a strong need for everything to proceed as planned
outcomes: Increased anxiety and sense of frustration
Decreased enjoyment of and satisfaction with life

manifestations: Lives alone, with no immediate family nearby
Strained relationships with friends and not sharing negative thoughts, subjectively feeling hard to connect
outcomes: Lack of emotional support and increased subjective sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains impulses originally meant to be expressed outward or to seek others' help, and instead acts on the self, digesting the energy inwardly.
manifestations: Does not share negative thoughts with friends; chooses to bear them alone
When plans are disrupted, directs energy into inner worry and self-blame rather than external communication or adjustment

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection, involving excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Rigid demands that things 'go according to plan'; excessive self-restriction
Blaming poor condition and loss of control on oneself, worrying that deviating from the plan will lead to collapse

exception_events.target_problem: When weather or plans change, He Nan usually develops catastrophic thinking (such as 'the weekend is ruined'), then feels anxious and frustrated and gives up looking for alternative activities.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On a few weekends, although it did not snow, he still found interesting things to do indoors; the weekend was not completely ruined, and the experience was better than expected.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: turning to indoor activities as a substitute; different understanding: observed that the actual outcome was not a disaster, thereby weakening the previous extreme prediction.

positive_force: Positive attitude, willing to try and cooperate with counseling
Able to recognize and acknowledge counterexamples (having found indoor fun on a snowless weekend)
Has some social support (a few friends to talk with)
negative_force: Marked tendency toward catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking
Low tolerance for change and uncertainty, over-relying on rigid plans
The physical strain from night shifts and sleep disturbance worsens negative emotions
Tending to avoid sharing and seeking support, leading to interpersonal tension and feelings of isolation

target_behavior.behavior: When plans or weather change, catastrophic thinking appears accompanied by marked anxiety and irritability
antecedent: Plans disrupted (such as weather not as expected)
Being scheduled for consecutive night shifts or having the schedule changed temporarily
target_behavior.core_reason: Low tolerance for change and uncertainty, forming the catastrophic prediction 'as long as it does not go according to plan it will be completely terrible' and all-or-nothing thinking.
target_behavior.function: Escapes uncertainty by rehearsing the worst case and rigid control, attempting to gain a sense of safety and control.
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep is disturbed, work performance declines, interpersonal relationships are strained, and interest in previously enjoyed activities is lost.

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep patterns are disturbed by negative thinking and anxiety (difficulty falling asleep, decreased sleep quality)
antecedent: Night-shift work leads to circadian rhythm disruption
Strong rumination and worry after a plan change
Before sleep, repeatedly thinking negative content such as 'the weekend will be ruined'
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and fortune-telling cognition raise physiological arousal, making it hard to relax and fall asleep.
target_behavior.function: Uses worry and controlling thinking to try to prevent uncertain consequences, but actually worsens insomnia.
target_behavior.consequence: Increased fatigue, impaired work performance, mood more prone to fluctuation and lowness.
